mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding 12 months raises the cost of capital, depressing corporate earnings and equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.5% quarter-over-quarter for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) signals weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to lower S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both above 12-month averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.7%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp month-over-month decline in initial jobless claims (reverse proxy via PAYEMS) below its 6-month average, combined with a concurrent drop in retail sales (HOUST), signals a sudden contraction in consumer activity, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both fall month-over-month and below 6-month averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 40% of triggered events.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 5% during a period of stable or rising consumer prices (CPIAUCSL) indicates stagflation risk, which erodes corporate pricing power and profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 5% and CPIAUCSL flat or rising for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 35% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent quarterly expansion in real GDP (GDPC1) above 3% for three consecutive quarters signals robust economic growth, which supports higher corporate earnings and justifies higher equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days in any macro regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.7%) in at least 60% of triggered quarters.
